title: Palamuti bignay: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Palamuti bignay: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Palamuti bignay is a bignay variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Palamuti is a registered bignay variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2002 as NSIC 2002 Bg 01.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Palamuti bignay is grown

blocks.text: Compare it with the others in our [bignay variety finder](/crop-varieties), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Palamuti was about 13 to 15 years old and about 4 meters tall when it was registered. It bears every year, with fruit in July August. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

A fruit of Palamuti weighs about 0.3 grams, and its shape is irregular spheroid. The flesh is reddish purple and smooth. Its sweetness measured 8.2 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 70 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is July August, bearing annual.
Where and when to plant Palamuti bignay

Pick a variety by the fruit your buyers pay for: its size, sweetness and flesh, and how regularly the tree bears. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Palamuti?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
